The star formation rate (SFR) is a fundamental property of galaxies, typically estimated via spectral energy distribution (SED) fitting or photometric data. This study utilizes the benchmark test of SFR derived from the benchmark line $\lambda$2479 (Brackett-$\gamma$) to evaluate the accuracy of these methods. We analyzed 134 nearby galaxies ($z \leq 0.1$) with high-quality, high-resolution spectroscopy to derive robust SFR estimates. By comparing these benchmark values against those obtained through SED fitting based on the Galaxy and Evolution (GALAXEV) code, we found a significant discrepancy: the GALAXEV model systematically underestimated the true SFR by a factor of 2.5 to three. This bias is most pronounced in systems with high dust content ($\text{H}\beta$ emission line ratios) and low specific SFRs.

This article is the first in a two-part study dedicated to a newly defined class of type $II$ quantum subalgevals of $\mathfrn{sl}_N$, which find natural applications within quantum spin chain models. We establish the invariance under symmetries of these subalgevals regarding their regional modules defined on finite regions of the spin chains. The method leverages the properties and structures recently revealed in our preceding paper ($I$). We determine the explicit forms of these symmetry generators, which are also related to the generators found in the type $I$ quantum subalvals. The proof of these results relies on the properties and structures recently revealed. Our work sets the foundation for exploring how such symmetries influence module decomposition and the identification of regional charges in the forthcoming paper ($I$).

Universal principles underpinning the structure and evolution of dynamic systems remain a central focus of scientific inquiry. This work introduces \textit{Unique Approach for Universal Diffusion (UAUD)}, \ a \textit{data-driven}\ method that enables the separation of a system's state vector into two components: (1) a \textit{Unique Feature (UF)} specific to that system, representing its Unique Internal State (UIS), and (2) a \textit{Universal Feature (Uf)} inherent to all dynamic systems, defining their Universal Diffusion Characteristics (UDC). While the Uf follows a \textit{Universal Law for Diffusion (ULD)}, this law is encoded in the Uf\ with a single \textit{Universal Parameter (UP)} that applies across all dynamic systems, in contrast to \textit{system-specific parameters}\ that currently require separate identification for each system. The Uf serves as a \textit{Universal Time (UT)} alongside the UF as \textit{Unique Feature Time (UFT)}. By leveraging UAUD, researchers can transform raw data into these two distinct parameters, allowing the Uf (Universal Time) to standardize the analysis of dynamic systems across different fields such as biology, chemistry, and physics. This framework enables direct comparison between systems by normalizing their temporal dynamics onto a \textit{Universal Time}\ scale, facilitating the identification of common scientific principles.

Recognizing handwritten mathematical expressions is crucial for digitizing historical scientific literature, a current challenge that hinders the extraction of knowledge from older publications. While deep learning has significantly advanced the field of expression recognition, it relies predominantly on printed text images, which are inadequate for facilitating the natural language processing necessary to convert regions containing handwriting into usable data. To address this gap, we introduce the HME-RD dataset, the first collection of handwritten mathematical expressions sensor-driven set. This corpus was gathered via a tablet application that records precise stroke coordinates, enabling the data to support rather than hinder natural language processing workflows. The sensor information within the HME-RD dataset allows for interactive recognition, a capability that paves the way for integrating human-computer interaction and computer-aided design technologies into the field of expression recognition.

This paper introduces a technique for generating synthetic speech durations using a neural network that operates outside statistical frameworks. The model is trained on the GigaSpeech test dataset's length set and demonstrates that a mid-layer from a time-step specific sub-network, paired with a non-linear function, effectively captures the distribution of synthetic speech lengths. The transformation maps this intermediate output to the full range of possible speech lengths through a median- and mean-based standardization step followed by an exponential function. When compared against standard statistical methods, this approach achieves comparable WER rates on the GigaSpeech ASR evaluation set and exhibits superior performance on the ITI-Reads task from the TTS track within the same challenge.

Spatial modeling is essential for understanding species distributions and forecasting the impacts of environmental change. While R offers a diverse collection of packages for single-species distribution modeling, the landscape is less developed for methods incorporating spatial data for multiple species or for integrated spatial modeling approaches. This manuscript introduces **spHabitat**, a comprehensive package designed to address these specific gaps by supporting various spatial modeling strategies for one or many species, including maximum entropy models, spatially explicit maximum entropy models, spatially explicit occupancy models, spatially explicit presence-absence models, and spatially explicit integrated models for presence data. We demonstrate the package's utility using simulated presence-only, presence-absence, occupancy, and integrated datasets, alongside applications to real-world data for American Black Bear, Eastern Chipmunk, and Northern Flying Squirrel. Finally, we explore spatial relationships among these co-occurring species through environmental niche overlap and pairwise comparisons.

Skin lesions are a significant cause of morbidity and mortality, with melanoma being the most common and dangerous form, often resulting in fatal metastasis if detected late. Early identification is critical for improving patient outcomes, yet the visual presentation of lesions is highly variable, posing a significant challenge for diagnosis. To address this, we introduce the Skincare initiative, an interactive machine learning platform designed to assist dermatologists in the differential diagnosis of skin lesions. Leveraging the vast dataset available from the Internet Medical Image Database (IMIDB), which houses hundreds of thousands of dermoscopic photographs, Skincare employs a generative adversarial network (GAN) to create dermoscopic images. These synthesized photographs are then used to enhance the doctor's assessment capabilities.

We introduce a stochastic autoencoder designed to forecast future spectra for Type Ia supernovae following the analysis of current spectrum data. This architecture features two key probabilistic layers: one governing latent representation distributions and another governing output (reconstruction) distributions. Utilizing simulated spectrum data, we assessed performance and identified an optimal stochastic weighting. We further examined how varying levels of stochasticity influence both the model's forecasting accuracy and the nature of learned latent features. Finally, we applied findings from these experiments to explore potential future research avenues.

We present the discovery of three spatially resolved neutral gas outflows, detected via Hα emission, surrounding a dusty star-forming galaxy at redshift z = 2.09 that exhibits significant gravitational lensing. The outflows display average velocities of approximately 200–300 km/s and cover a spatial extent of roughly 400–500 pc. By comparing these measurements to simulations, we find that the outflows are best explained by galactic winds generated from clustered supernovae rather than AGN activity. The total mass of the outflows is comparable to the mass ejected by the galaxy's stellar population, indicating that the majority of the galaxy's momentum feedback occurs through these neutral gas outflows.

This study examines the turbulent free plume generated by a turbulent, buoyant jet entering a quiescent environment, focusing on the incorporation of passive scalars and particles with varying densities. Plume structures were analyzed using both numerical simulations, which solved the full Eulerian Navier-Stokes equations, and large-eddy simulations (LES). To specifically target the near-field region where initial conditions heavily influence outcomes, both approaches utilized inflow data from a highly resolved direct numerical simulation (DNS). These results indicate that, despite the expectation that passive scalars and dense particles behave similarly, the mean plume exhibits distinct differences between the two. Notably, the density ratio at which the local mean entrainment rate for plume-travelling particles matches the incorporation rate of scalars is approximately 1.1 in the near-field. Furthermore, both the numerical simulations and LES demonstrate that the mean entrainment trend converges toward predictions found in extensive literature for buoyant far-field plumes. This consistency with established far-field data confirms that the specific initial and boundary conditions used in this work successfully generate a realistic near-field structure that accurately transitions to the standard far-field regime.

Graphs fail to capture multi-way interactions prevalent in systems ranging from coevolution and ecological competitions to social gatherings and epidemics. Although extant spectral theories for hypergraphs have addressed basic properties, their impact on complex dynamics remains underexplored. This study introduces the use of spectral tools to analyze disease extinction within hypergraph-based populations, accounting for simultaneous multi-individual infections. Our findings establish robust lower bounds on the extinction rate, linking it to spectral properties of a specific generator. These results are applicable to various infection mechanisms and demonstrate that, conceptually, hypergraph dispersions accelerate epidemic fade-out comparable to homogeneous mixing.

This work theoretically examines the impact of magnetic exchange, spin-orbit coupling, and chirality on the magnetic textures of two-dimensional (2D) ferromagnets, utilizing an Indium submonolayer chromium iodide bilayer as a specific case. We identify that the interplay between these factors can generate two distinct ferromagnetic configurations: a conventional uniform state and a vortex-like configuration. Notably, this vortex-like arrangement is predicted to emerge only when spin-orbit coupling and chirality are present. Furthermore, we demonstrate that within such vortex-like ferromagnetism, the Rashba effect acts as a pivotal mechanism, capable of producing giant magnetization anisotropy. These findings offer essential insights into understanding and controlling complex magnetic behaviors in van der Waals 2D ferromagnetic materials.

Differential rotation serves as a primary driver of magnetic activity in solar-type stars, yet its precise dynamical influence remains debated. While differential rotation in the Sun is generally considered to be driven by convection, the situation in solar analogs differs, as these stars typically lack the strong differential rotation seen in the Sun and instead exhibit anti-solar rotation gradients, where angular velocity increases toward the surface. This study investigates the impact of such dynamics on magnetic cycles using magnetic simulations with modified Laplace-expectation (LE) boundary conditions. We find that systems lacking differential rotation or featuring anti-solar gradients still generate magnetic cycles; however, these cycles are characterized by greater magnetic field amplitudes, more frequent activity bursts, and more frequent magnetic reversals. These active regions are primarily attributed to the magnetic flapping process, which is intensified by the absence of solar-style differential rotation or the presence of anti-solar gradients. Consequently, we conclude that magnetic cycles in solar-type stars are not solely dependent on differential rotation, suggesting they may persist even in the the rotation profiles of gradually rotating stars.

Multimodal deep frameworks have become a research priority due to their ability to leverage information across diverse inputs for superior performance. Existing methods, however, are constrained by their reliance on specific input configurations, such as specific node counts or network topologies. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel Generalized K-fan (GKF) architecture. This new framework is highly adaptable, supporting variable numbers of input types and specific network structures. We evaluated the proposed GKG on several standard datasets, comparing its results against current top-performing multidimensional models. This evaluation included a comprehensive analysis of performance, per-input contributions, and internal representations. Results demonstrate that the new GKF framework not only delivers enhanced predictive accuracy but also provides deeper insights into both the contributions of distinct input types and the high-level features learned by the model.

Model checking is a standard software analysis method that verifies if a program's state space conforms to specified properties. To address the exponential growth of this state space, state-space reduction techniques have been developed, with Dependency Graphs (DPG) emerging as a prominent approach capable of eliminating vast portions of the state space—often exceeding what other methods can achieve—for multithreaded programs utilizing fine-grained locking. These techniques have been integrated into several toolsets, with two primary DPG implementations, mcmini and comcheck, showing significant advancements. Although both tools have contributed to enhancements, their results have not been directly compared. This paper presents Mcmini, a new model checker written in the mcmini environment that features modular architecture to facilitate research into various state removal strategies. By providing a customizable framework for debugging protocols, Mcmini allows investigators to evaluate multiple hypotheses regarding effective state pruning. We detail several strategies tested within this framework and demonstrate that their combined usage achieves performance gains comparable to comcheck's results

WhatsApp has introduced features to identify and flag forwardable messages, yet the effectiveness of limiting message forwarding in stopping the spread of misinformation remains largely unexamined. This study investigates this gap using a series of controlled field experiments conducted via WhatsApp groups among participants in Buenos Aires, Argentina. The results indicate that restricting forwarding has no measurable impact on misinformation dissemination. Additionally, controlled expository interventions have little effect unless they are tailored to a recipient's specific political preferences. While these findings do not suggest that limiting forwarding helps combat falsehoods, they do demonstrate that in-group corrections work best when personalized. Consequently, these outcomes offer valuable insights for refining future efforts to mitigate the propagation of misinformation.

We analyze a model of a neutral branching population featuring an infinite allele system where new alleles arise through mutation. In an infinite-allele framework, mutation replaces an existing allele at a locus with a previously unseen one. We examine allele frequencies for arbitrary types, focusing on scenarios where the expected number of offspring per individual exceeds one (a supercritical expected reproduction function $m(z)$). We derive asymptotic formulas for the Allele Prevalence Spectrum (APS)—the distribution describing how many bear a specific allele. Our approach considers three distinct dynamical regimes: (1) a case where $m(z)=1+\beta z$ for some $\beta>0$, yielding formulas aligned with Laplace transforms of the branching process; (2) a case where $m(z)=1+\beta z^q$ for some $0<q<1$, where formulas involve special functions; (3) a case where $m(z)=\alpha z^q$ for some $\alpha>0$ and $q>1$, where formulas rely on stable branching attractors. We support these findings with simulations using a single-locus, infinite-allele branching model to illustrate the theoretical results.

This research introduces a novel system for detecting audio spoofing attacks using Deep Learning (DL), which was evaluated in the NIST 2020 Logical Nonsense Statement Competition (NLS-ST 2020). To enhance detection capabilities, the system integrates two key innovations: a Recurrent Attention Unit (RAU) and a Spectral Attention Unit (SAU). The RAU functions by refining the recurrent features extracted from an Echo State Network (ESN), while the SAU selectively emphasizes critical frequency components within the spectral dimension of DL representations. Both units work in conjunction with an ESN to optimize the system for end-to-end spoofing detection. Testing on the SECMARK 2020 dataset demonstrated that this proposed architecture significantly outperforms both standalone ESN models and previous state-of-the-art solutions specifically tailored for NLS-SP.

We investigate supersymmetric inflationary models that remain supersymmetric only at the single-loop level, utilizing the effective field theory framework. By applying supersymmetry constraints within this approach, we estimate quantum corrections to inflationary observables, yielding predictions for scalar amplitude, tensor-to-scurity ratio, and spectral index that align well with Planck mission data. Our analysis indicates that quantum corrections significantly influence inflationary predictions, particularly the scalar amplitude, by one order of magnitude. Consequently, when seeking low-energy signatures of supersymmetry, such as effective single-field descriptions, it is essential to incorporate these quantum contributions.

We introduce an innovative approach for analyzing second-order quantum interference patterns in photon pair experiments. This methodology uncovers an asymmetry in the correlation functions of entangled photon pairs, enabling a more precise determination of the phase. This refinement enhances the test of Bell's inequalities and significantly reduces measurement uncertainties. By redefining the measurement protocol, the associated error is diminished by a factor of four, and the computed precision now aligns closely with the theoretical limit.

Superconducting quantum circuits built from microwave-frequency resonators and transmission line components on shared substrate form essential blocks for universal quantum computing. These systems rely on near-field terahertz microscopy to investigate quasiparticle excitations and flux-induced defects that cause qubit decoherence. However, achieving the necessary spectral accuracy and spatial precision for quantitative analysis has been an obstacle. This work demonstrates a calibrated near-field technique that provides Terahertz spectral access with 0.15 THz accuracy and spatial resolution of 0.3 wavelengths at the terahertz frequency. By examining how microwave resonators respond under these terahertz conditions, we validate the approach for performing quantitative microscopies.

The real line is partitioned into maximal nested families of subsets, where each element in this partition corresponds to a specific collection type. Assuming every element in these families is measurable under some fixed tone for measurable sets, we prove that each collection must be null. This result implies that if one were to assume all such elements are measurable, they would all necessarily be measurable of a particular null kind. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the same conclusion applies even when dropping requirements and considering arbitrary collections of real numbers in these nested families. These conclusions rely fundamentally on specific properties inherent in the magnitude of the reals.

We examine how strategic interactions between a passive, high-frequency market-maker and a group of active, slower traders with heterogeneous strategies impact financial performance. The active agents employ a mix of trend-following and mean-reverting approaches, while the passive agent acts as an arbitrageur who adjusts sizing based on anticipated active flows and trend or mean characteristics. The analysis reveals that while active performance is generally suppressed by their mutual behavior, the dominant active strategy remains robust only in cases where agents diversify across both trend-following and mean-reversion methods. Conversely, clear signs of interaction are more likely when agents are uniformly mean-reverted. The passive agent's optimal approach is to act as an arbitrageur targeting active flows, with performance driven by the specific reaction to dominant trends or mean shifts chosen by active participants. The study underscores that the "passive" label is often misleading, as these market participants typically realize higher returns than the active traders they exploit.

Protocol identification stands as a core function for traffic-based network defense strategies, yet recent years have seen a surge in research targeting these identification protocols. The present study examines current vulnerabilities by introducing novel test cases and attack vectors, while also outlining methods to strengthen the protocol defense of two prominent open-source tools, Snort and Suricata.

Placing a superconductor adjacent to a magnonic material generates effective, static magnetic fields at their interface, arising from inductive coupling of the superconductor's surface currents with the magnetic medium. These fields interact with the Mészáros effect, enabling the superconductor to function as a dynamic gate for magnons. This approach provides a versatile framework for integrating and controlling magnetism using purely superconducting technologies, facilitating the development of hybrid quantum devices that combine these two systems.

Federated learning and classification with unknown categories are two separate fields; this paper addresses them simultaneously. It examines training zero-shot classifiers with never-seen categories on clients that lack labels for those new categories, presenting a novel zero-shot framework to overcome data silos and classification gaps. By splitting traditional training into phased strategies, this approach retracts previously trained local models as baseline predictions to calculate novel category baselines, which are then utilized to refine global models. Experiments on AudioSet using the YACO benchmark demonstrate that the proposed method substantially outperforms existing solutions for zero-shot audio classification and shows strong generalization in real-world scenarios.

This study introduces an advanced protocol for verifying multi-qubit entangled states across high dimensions. The proposed method builds upon the generalized measurement operators—functioning as extensions of the Pauli matrices for dimensions $d>2$—to achieve comprehensive entanglement verification through a strategy equivalent in thoroughness to the original Pauli-based approach for qubits. The feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed protocol were confirmed experimentally using the trapped ion system at Jyotiion, successfully generating a Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state comprising seven ququarts (ion logical states of dimension seven). The experimental data demonstrated fidelity exceeding 99% and thoroughly validated the proposed verification method.

This work investigates channel estimation for coupled Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS)-aided multi-user systems employing Coordinated Multi-Antenna receivers, where the lack of hardware beamers necessitates separate estimation for each IRS link and user link, consuming significant pilot resources. To mitigate this, we propose a low-complexity design leveraging coupled channel estimation through distributed pilots, ensuring orthogonality at the receiver to simplify the process. Under constraints of available pilot count, we maximize the system's sum rate by jointly optimizing the IRS configuration and pilot allocation, addressing the resulting non-concave challenge with a convergent algorithm based on successive convex approximation and orthogonalization techniques. Furthermore, we address computational overhead by developing a cascaded channel estimation approach that utilizes a single receiver for all IRS units, thereby enabling a smart pilot strategy through smart beam alignment to enhance performance. Finally, we demonstrate that our suggested algorithm outperforms existing methods in terms of both computational efficiency and system sum rate.

This study examines U.S. regional news coverage of COVID-19 using data from 211 domains of the NewsDirect consortium between April 2021 and January 2022. It analyzes time-series patterns in news volume relative to case rates, fatalities, and audience size across regions. While similar correlations between news density and health outcomes exist nationwide, these relationships fluctuate significantly by region and over time. The analysis reveals a disparity between regional digital news outlets and national outlets like CNN and the New York Times, which prioritize audience figures; conversely, the study finds virtually no link between COVID-related coverage and actual newspaper circulation. Critically, the evidence suggests that regional digital news density is unrelated to reported fatalities or cases, even after adjusting for the variability of these correlations by region and period. These findings challenge existing literature suggesting a connection between media coverage and individual or aggregate behaviors, and the lack of association with print circulation indicates distinct operational dynamics within regional digital news markets.

Neural networks are increasingly recognized for their ability to simulate human cognitive processes, specifically regarding memory and its role in complex tasks. This study examines whether equipping a neural network with Hebbian associative memory enhances performance in a proposed artificial task that mimics natural human counting. Findings indicate that integrating memory into the network significantly boosts task performance compared to standard models without memory. Moreover, by analyzing network activations, we demonstrate that the network explicitly stores numerical values within its memory mechanism, providing compelling evidence that stored information drives the improved performance. Ultimately, this research highlights the value of incorporating explicit memory mechanisms in tasks demanding sequential decision-making based on sustained information.

Bloom filters are compact space-efficient data structures used for rapidly verifying if an element belongs to a set, offering a "yes" or no answer, with the sole limitation of potentially yielding false positives. Cuckoo filters were introduced to resolve these false positives, yet they cannot confirm membership with total certainty while maintaining comparable space efficiency during high-load scenarios. This work introduces Xor filters, a novel filter structure capable of definitively saying "yes" or "no," with the added capability of predicting the precise location of any inserted element. Evaluated results demonstrate that for identical storage capacities, Xor filters are substantially more compact than Bloom filters and equally space-efficient as Cuckoo filters, ultimately delivering superior speed and space performance for filtering operations that require confirmation.

This expository note highlights various links within the analysis of convex functions and their derivatives at the boundary, the Brunn-Minkowski theory, and the theory of harmonic and pluriharmonic functions along with their boundary behaviors.

This study examines how market price trends are influenced by a stream of future trades, considering time, execution cost, and volume as key attributes. The trade data is modeled as an ordered sequence of quadruples: (time, price, cost, volume). The analysis utilizes a specific metric to quantify the impact of past trades on future price movements, represented as the $L_2$-norm of the aggregate trade intensity function. Using standard mean reversion theory, it is demonstrated that the variance associated with price changes declines as the L2 norm of the trade intensity function increases, thereby establishing a direct link between trading activity and price variance. The study also addresses the endogeneity of trade timing, showing that this factor has negligible effects on the overall conclusions. Furthermore, it is proven that the proposed measure remains robust to the sequence in which trade information is revealed.

This article introduces FLVoogd, a robust federated learning framework designed to defend against malicious attacks while preserving the privacy of user parameters. The framework begins by employing a novel, privacy-preserving technique for selecting clients, ensuring privacy is maintained even when participation data is exposed during the selection process. Once clients are chosen, a new server-side anomaly detection mechanism is utilized to identify and exclude malicious users from training. This approach offers a significant advantage by keeping malicious user parameters private, in contrast to conventional methods that often require the server to access this sensitive information. Finally, to protect client privacy during anomaly detection, we implement a secure computation protocol that allows clients to keep their sensitive model weights confidential.

Simulated-to-realized transfer learning (Sim2Real) is an essential strategy for deploying robotics algorithms in actual environments. This approach involves training a model on physical quantities collected via real-world scenarios and then transferring that knowledge to operate effectively in other distinct real environments. This study centers on navigating agents using a "what-where-how" framework, where the agent determines its next movement based on current visual inputs and environmental context without requiring manual labeling. To validate this, we introduce a gradient-based method that significantly enhances a model's adaptability when encountering new, unseen real-world settings. By simulating diverse ground truth variations during the simulation phase, we enable the agent to better generalize. This technique eliminates the expensive and labor-intensive requirement for additional training data across every target environment. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms state-of-the-art methods, achieving superior navigation success rates in simulated-to-real deployment.

Deepfake technology has recently emerged as an increasingly urgent issue, resulting in numerous identitiy theft incidents and disinformation spreading. These synthetic videos typically rely heavily on source material from internet clips with a tight focus on faces within the upper torso. This paper presents an innovative deepfake framework designed to operate on such constrained datasets. Specifically, we propose a dual-stage architecture: the initial stage employs a generative adversarial network to synthesize a single speaker profile picture by fusing face regions extracted from the target with the expression dynamics from another source; the subsequent stage upcasts this generated face picture while preserving the background context of the original footage. Crucially, this process occurs without any requirement for pre-training models or additional supervised annotations. We also introduce an upscaling module tailored to maintain background stability during the resolution enhancement process. Comprehensive experiments conducted across two public datasets and a newly collected private dataset validate the effectiveness of our approach. Moreover, we introduce an identification system built on a lightweight, trained ResNet model that achieves superior anti-forgery performance.

The study of sub-Neptune-sized exoplanets with temperate climates remains a major focus in exoplanet research, as their internal structures and compositional makeup are often ambiguous. This work presents a new approach to modeling the atmospheres and interiors of these planets, aiming to determine whether their fluids exist in a supercritical state or as a liquid-gas equilibrium. We examine how this distinction influences the optical depth associated with cloud formation and how that cloud layer modulates the observable transit signals. Our analysis reveals that when supercritical conditions prevail, supercritical solubility balance dictates cloud composition and optical depth, a mechanism that can obscure the detection of ocean worlds. Conversely, if liquid-gas equilibrium holds true, traditional gas thermodynamic controls on cloud properties and transit signatures remain intact. These findings highlight that accurately characterizing temperate sub-Neptunes requires planetary models that incorporate the fundamental physics of their internal states.

This paper explores the feasibility of learning attractors that correspond to biological plausibility within a Spiking Neural Network (BBSN) for performing associative memory. By employing a local Hebbian rule to implement attractor dynamics, we first demonstrate that although stable limit cycles can be generated, they fail to align with stable conditions observed in biological systems. Consequently, a modified learning rule is proposed to overcome these limitations and enhance biological compatibility. We further demonstrate this approach via a simulation of a two-dimensional continuous BBSN employing circular connectivity, where we examine the system's response to inputs representing heads, tails, and various orientations of eight distinct animals.

This challenge focuses on predicting a set of synonyms for each of a selected 1,000 words, a task deliberately designed to be arduous by utilizing only a small portion of the standard "Gold Standard" found in the WordNet lexicon. The study presents a detailed analysis of the human baseline and four distinct computational approaches: two involving traditional methods and two employing deep learning models. The findings offer valuable insights for researchers developing systems to construct challenge tasks that are particularly difficult yet solvable.

This study introduces an efficient approach for dynamically verifying A posteriori stochastic models based on Chaos Expansion methods using generalized (CGP). A key feature of proposed strategy is its ability to consider only a few points compared global behavior, estimating remainder term during simulation process. We compare two approaches for estimating this error: first one involves constructing deterministic bound based on model specific constraints; second utilizes statistical methods by evaluating residual statistics sample. Both strategies ensure computational efficiency while providing guarantee global control uncertainty, with extensive tests demonstrating performance.

This paper introduces a sequential alteration identification and isolation (SAII) framework designed for systems where high-dimensional trends are only partially visible. Unlike existing approaches, which are limited to scenarios with complete trend visibility, our method effectively captures trends across all dimensions while operating within a partial observability setting. Specific modifications to the classic SAII algorithm are proposed, including a new score-based technique for identifying significant changes and a revised isolation strategy that filters out noise. The method's validity is confirmed through applications on both simulated data and real-world financial stock records.

We have conducted a comprehensive study of 12 dwarf galaxies, focusing on their star formation histories and chemical enrichment patterns by analyzing 120 red giant branch (RGB) stars with high-resolution spectra. By applying isochrone fitting and chemical abundance modeling, we determined the star formation history and metal enrichment trajectory for each galaxy. Our findings indicate that 10 of the 12 galaxies exhibit a single, early burst of star formation occurring within the first 100 Myr, characterized by an early metal enrichment rate of approximately $\Delta$[Fe]/[Fe]=0.2–0.3 dex per century of solar mass, with the remaining two showing more extended formation timescales. The observed chemical patterns in these dwarfs are consistent with an early burst scenario, supporting the conclusion that most of these systems formed the majority of their stellar populations within the first 100 Myr.

Although multi-modal conditional random fields (M-CRFs) have proven highly effective for digitizing complex, visually dense documents, they demand extensive labeling costs. Because document templates often vary significantly, applying template-based labeling to heterogeneous documents results in high labeling expenses. To address this, we introduce a multi-modal active learning framework designed to minimize both time and financial costs associated with multi-modal labeling. Our approach integrates two key components: a similarity model for identifying visually comparable regions and a diversity model for locating varied visual features. These models work together to prioritize labeling efforts on data points that would otherwise be excluded during passive sampling. We evaluated our system against state-of-the-art extractors using three public benchmarks, achieving cost reductions of 80% to 95% without compromising extraction accuracy.

We employ density functional theory to investigate the influence of various interface atomic configurations on the electronic arrangement at the EuS/InAs interfaces. Our findings reveal that specific configurations induce a pronounced spin-splitting sub-bands near the Fermi level within the InAs, driven by strong hybridization between Eu 5d and In 4p orbitals. Additionally, we observe that the electronic arrangement at these interfaces is highly sensitive to specific atomic arrangements. Notably, a interface with an antiferromagnetic EuS exhibits an interface with a magnetic arrangement, producing distinct magnetic arrangements. At the same atomic arrangement, we find that the atomic arrangement at the interface with a ferromagnetic arrangement exhibits weak magnetic arrangements. We conclude that a magnetic arrangement with an antiferromagnetic arrangement exhibits a magnetic arrangement, while other configurations do not.

Training deep neural networks (DNNs) using deep learning frameworks has become integral to modern AI, yet the sheer complexity of these models often necessitates substantial hardware resources. As DNN architectures continue to grow, researchers are increasingly exploring intrinsic DNN pruning methods to reduce model size and enhance inference speed while retaining accuracy. Although promising, these techniques introduce significant overhead during the joint DNN co-design and training phases. Current approaches rely on coarse, layer-by-layer connections that result in dense subgraphs, complicating efficient execution on standard hardware. We propose **ClickTrain**, an end-to-end training framework designed to simplify and accelerate the entire co-design process. ClickTrain achieves this by leveraging fine-grained, architecture-preserving DNN pruning to generate a sparse subgraph with low degree. This enables fast, scalable training on consumer-grade machines by transforming the problem into one of selecting an optimal sparse training architecture. We formulate this selection as an integer linear programming (ILP) problem and employ a series of effective heuristics to ensure near-optimality. Empirical results demonstrate that ClickTrain successfully trains various models—including ResNet-50, BERT-base, and Transformer-XL—using as little as 16 GB of RAM on standard laptops, delivering competitive performance.

Neutron star–black hole (NS‑BH) mergers are anticipated as a prevalent outcome of stellar evolution and are expected to generate gravitational waves (GWs) detectable by current interferometers like LIGO, Virgo, and KAGRA. While general relativity allows these events to produce GW signals similar to binary neutron star (NS‑NS) mergers, the lack of definitive “smoking gun” evidence distinguishes NS‑BH from NS‑NS events. Consequently, accurately classifying NS‑BH mergers is essential for determining the demographics of compact-object mergers in the universe. In this work, we introduce a machine-learning algorithm designed to identify and categorize GW signals from NS‑BH events across all phases of a merger event.

"Transiting the system TOI-5542, the exoplanet TOI-5542 b orbits a metal-deficient G-type host star as a hot Jupiter. Confirming this candidate's status, we gathered a comprehensive dataset comprising 131 high-precision photometric measurements from TESS, PLATO, and ground-based telescopes, alongside 13 new high-resolution spectroscopic observations. Our analysis reveals a highly eccentric orbit (e = 0.21 ± 0.03) for a planet with a mass of 0.88 ± 0.09 MJup and a radius of 1.12 ± 0.05 RJup, which circulates at a period of 3.53 days around a 5.63-Gyr-old star. TOI-5542 b stands as one of the few known hot Jupiters exhibiting such significant eccentricity and ranks among the oldest of its kind. Additionally, our study identifies a 3σ non-sinusoidal variation in the planet's transit light curve, suggesting the presence of a 0.14-degree orbital inclination relative to our line of sight. While the cause of this eccentricity remains unclear, we explore the possibility that it resulted from past secular gravitational interactions with another, now-lost planet."

This paper investigates reinforcement learning within restricted Markov decision processes (RLRMDPs), a framework where transition transition probabilities are constrained to lie within a predefined structure. In RLMDPs, sample complexity scales only logarithmically with the state and state space sizes, offering substantial theoretical gains over standard Markov decision processes. While previous research established sample complexity bounds for these problems using techniques from standard MDP theory, this approach proves inefficient for tasks requiring high sample counts. Addressing this gap, we introduce a novel dual-based primal-dual proximal alternating regularized decomposition (PPAD) algorithm. This method leverages the problem's specific structure to achieve sample scales that are logarithmic in state space dimensions. Furthermore, our theoretical results for these PPAD-based methods are nearly optimal, improving upon existing bounds by a square-root factor.

This paper outlines an approach to identifying handwritten mathematical notation, outlining both the challenges involved and how machine learning can help address them. Notation recognition carries greater difficulty than text recognition due to symbols possessing multiple potential meanings contingent on their context. We detail the implementation of deep-learning-based text recognition to address this domain, achieving significant performance gains. Furthermore, we propose an approach to leveraging the known surrounding text to refine symbol identification, significantly enhancing overall results. By integrating these symbolic dependencies into the recognition process, we achieve meaningful improvements.

We investigate the expansion of B-cohomology for Lefschetz primitives under the action of the Lie derivative associated with the canonical connection on the canonical bundle. In the context of a hyperKähler manifold, this operation is equivalent to computing the Chern character of an appropriate holomorphic vector space sheaf defined on a specific family of complex structures. Furthermore, we demonstrate that for any complete Kähler manifold, this operation aligns with B-cohomology derived from primitive elements satisfying a generalized Lefschetz condition, thereby extending our analysis to apply within non-singular projective algebraic geometry and to Riemannian Kähler manifolds subject to Einstein conditions. As a derived application, we establish a characterization of which cohomology classes persist unchanged during the continuous deformation of the complex structure on a projective manifold.

Social networks serve as interaction systems where individuals act as nodes and relationships function as links; however, these structures are dynamic, undergoing continuous evolution. In this paper, we investigate the statistical properties of the time intervals between interactions—defined as the duration from one relationship's initiation to the next—across various social networks. Our findings indicate that these intervals adhere to a power-law distribution characterized by an exponent ranging between 1.0 and 1.5. Furthermore, we observe that this exponent correlates with interaction complexity, a metric derived from network degree distribution and structural motifs. To explain these results, we propose a model demonstrating that the emergence of power-law distributed durations results from the superposition of multiple exponential processes.

This study introduces a novel actor-critic reinforcement learning algorithm, termed "Deep Hamiltonian Policy Gradient" (DHGP), designed to tackle continuous control tasks. By integrating the Metropolis Heat Algorithm (MHA)—a variant employed for sampling from complex probability distributions—into the policy gradient framework, DHGP enables the learner to draw diverse actions from the current policy's distribution rather than relying solely on greedy or single-sample selections. This mechanism helps mitigate issues such as distribution shift and excessive variance, which often degrade performance in standard deep RL methods. Additionally, we employ the MHA within the critic component to approximate the state value function more accurately. Experimental results across various benchmarks demonstrate that this new algorithm significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

A detailed description of a Stratified Navigation Controller (SNC) capable of managing the full spectrum of ship operations—from high-level mission planning to low-level actuator commands—is initially omitted. This paper presents the robust sonar integration scheme essential for the SNC, featuring both surface and subsurface layers to support collision avoidance. The proposed model-predictive collision avoidance algorithm leverages this sonar data, and the paper delivers a comprehensive analysis of the SNC through simulated scenarios.

Nereid, Neptune's third-largest moon, possesses a surface heavily influenced by volatile deposits likely delivered by active Triton ices. While recent studies modeled Nereid's visible and near-infrared reflectance using a two-component mixture of water ice and amorphous nitrogen ice, these neglected other volatile compounds abundant in Triton's geology. This work expands that model to a four-component system incorporating carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide, and methane ices alongside nitrogen. Our analysis indicates that current NIR data alone cannot distinguish between mixtures containing these various volatiles; consequently, additional spectral data from UV or mid-infrared ranges are required to constrain future compositional studies of this moon.

We present a new Bayesian strategy for optimizing treatments within Dynamic Treatment Regimens (DTRs), a concept applicable to sequential decision-making areas like operations research. Our approach incorporates a "pessimism" parameter to steer decisions away from purely reward-maximizing tactics, instead favoring strategies with lower risk variance. By drawing on the connection between these variance-near-zero rules and confidence intervals, our method can substantially outperform standard, non-pessimistic Bayesian frameworks when performance data is scarce. Specifically, it seeks to prevent suboptimal choices during the early phases of deployment by avoiding decisions supported by weak statistical evidence. The validity of this approach is established through a rigorous theoretical proof of its consistency and its practical efficacy is demonstrated via a simulation based on a DTR model for personalized healthcare.

This paper explores the application of homological invariants, specifically derived categories of module categories, in representing dualities found within the category of finite groups. The text highlights the significance of Morita equivalence and Hasegawa-Rouquier equivalence, with a focus on providing the foundational elements required for implementing these concepts through explicit derived functors applicable to Hasegawa-Rouquier dualities. The discussion concludes by outlining strategies for making these theoretical principles more concrete and applicable in practice.

We re-examine the non-contextual inequalities defined by Mermin using the complex $E_8$ root system to demonstrate a violation of these inequalities via contextual quantum strategies, achieving values as high as $10\sqrt{2}$ compared to a limit of that order. These strategy matrices are constructed from complex Hadamard matrices, which, unlike their real counterparts, lack real forms and exhibit properties of infinite sets similar to the real Hadamard matrices. Notably, our primary quantum protocol corresponds to $4\times 4$ matrices with entries $\pm 1/i$, yielding a maximum non-inequality violation of $4\sqrt{2}$.

Multiple-body bound states (MBS) emerging within flat energy bands have garnered significant interest due to their capacity for superconducting phases lacking traditional BCS mechanisms and their association with exotic anyonic statistics. This study proposes that in systems hosting multiple flat bands, MBS-driven superconductivity can manifest without requiring geometric frustration or the Mulsing effect. Instead, we demonstrate that MBS superconductivity can arise solely from competition among flat bands, a conclusion supported by theoretical modeling of two prototypical models: the Haldane and Moiré Hubbard frameworks. In the Haldane system, we reveal a fully gapped superconducting regime exhibiting properties of $p_x+ip$ superconductivity characterized by Majorana modes within the gap. In the Moiré system, we identify a fully gapped regime corresponding to $c$-wave superconductivity mediated by an $s$-wave pairing channel. Furthermore, we outline experimental protocols for verifying MBS-based superconductivity in both architectures.

Service portfolios and similar structures are frequently represented as existence-absence matrices, where rows correspond to services and columns to clients, indicating whether a specific service was rendered. This paper evaluates various service profiling clustering methods, noting that traditional algorithms based on distance or probabilistic models often fail because such data lacks an inherent geometric interpretation. Consequently, this study proposes and tests a hybrid model that integrates both an ex-absence matrix and a binary presence-only layer, which is then analyzed using a model-based approach. This technique leverages the flexibility of latent class analysis while providing parameters that can be interpreted to define service profiles. The proposed methodology is demonstrated through a non-experimental analysis of interviewed business clients' service usage.

Identifying salient objects is essential for various computer vision applications, including navigation, scene analysis, and detection. This study introduces a cohesive framework to locate and recognize salient items within RGB images, leveraging both handcrafted and deep features derived from regions of interest detected by state-of-the-art segmenters like Mask R-CNN. To enhance the system, we integrate feature fusion strategies and a cohesive regular term inspired by shape smoothness prior research. Furthermore, we propose a novel metric, "salient probability," derived from an RGB model trained on salient datasets, designed to function effectively even in RGB-only inputs by compensating for the lack of depth data. Tested on RGB images from the Salient Object Discovery (SOD) dataset as well as RGB slices from the Salient Object in Scene (SOS) dataset, the results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches, achieving the best results on RGB portions from the RGB half of the SOD dataset.

This study outlines the UM-Iu@LING participation in Team 6's OBSA challenge at SemEval-2019. Our primary objective is to identify hate speech and offensive language in Twitter posts. To achieve this, we developed a hybrid framework that integrates a BERT-based mechanism with a support vector machine (LSVM). This approach yielded the second-best performance for single-classification tasks, surpassing multi-classification methods.

Our investigation examines the ratios $p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are respectively the counts of palindromic and antipalindromic subwords within a fixed infinite sequence. We demonstrate that for every sequence containing at least one palindromic and one antipalindromic subword, this ratio converges to $p_0(q_0)$ as the length of the subwords approaches infinity; here $p_0$ and $q_0$ represent the total numbers of distinct palindromic and antipalindromic strings capable of specific structural properties within the sequence. Consequently, we derive several new identities regarding epimorphic sequences and identify all cases where the ratio remains constant at $1$.

Reconstructing tomographic images and identifying physical materials from polyenergetic X-ray data poses significant challenges due to absorption across diverse compositions and heterogeneous structures. Although reducing these X-ray sources to discrete energies simplifies the process, it can still fail accurately for materials with diverse sizes and may introduce artifacts. Conversely, utilizing monochromatic assumptions yields monotonically decreasing projections that allow background noise and artifacts to be treated as negative features during reconstruction, thereby corrupting the final outcome. In contrast, our proposed approach for handling polyenergetic datasets treats CT reconstruction and noise reduction as a unified task while simultaneously performing material breakdown analysis. We model the unknowns as multiple monochromatic images at distinct energy levels, imposing only mild non-negativity constraints. By defining a data-fidelity term based on polyenergetic system operators and a regularizer based on total variation, our convex variational framework is analyzed under differentiation rules for polyenergetic operators. Numerical experiments demonstrate the method's robustness across various scenarios, highlighting its potential for practical implementation in CT imaging and material identification systems.

Handwritten Text Recognition (HTR) is a highly valuable multilingual task with significant real-world applications. Despite the availability of large datasets for dominant languages like English, low-resource languages face data scarcity, preventing effective training of state-of-the-art models. Recently, data augmentation methods such as Stochastic Attention Synthesis (SAS) have enabled single-shot composition of new languages using a base high-resource language and a set of character symbols from which the low-resource language can be derived. This paper presents MultiSAS, an extension of SAS designed to simultaneously generate multiple low-resource languages at once. Our method retains the core advantages of single-shot approaches while significantly cutting production time and making multi-language data generation more practical. We evaluate MultiSAS on six additional languages across two major international benchmarks, the ICDAR 2013 Holistically Spelled Words (HSW) challenge and the ICDAR 2017 Handwriting Continual Competition (HCC). The results demonstrate that our approach surpasses single-language SAS variants and outperforms traditional data augmentation strategies.

This work reports on combined first-principles nuclear calculations involving deformed shell effects, mixing energies, and shape isomer contributions to the free energy of heavy nuclei, with specific attention to the region surrounding neutron-rich fissionable isotopes. The study reveals that the neutron drip line, when accounted for via the shell model, is notably more extended than previously indicated by droplet model approximations lacking such detailed structures. The analysis of the free energy landscape highlights the significance of multiple coexisting metastable shapes in heavy nuclei. Additionally, the effects of temperature and rotational motion on these structures are examined. The theoretical predictions regarding binding energies and neutron numbers are compared against experimental data, and potential energy surfaces are utilized to refine the boundaries of stability and the neutron drip line.

This study examines key aspects of topological quantum phenomena using the SSH (Su-Schrieffer-Heeger) model, a1D system. We define and discuss the significance of chiral and quantum numbers in this model. Topological phases are analyzed by measuring end-point states, with phase transitions identified through changes in energy gaps. Gaps close at transition points, leading to the emergence of metallic behavior. Transition points are further substantiated by energy distributions, which display symmetry breaking. Symmetry is monitored via the SSH Hamiltonian, allowing for phase separation. End-point states are identified using particle occupation numbers within distinct phases. Finally, we outline research directions, highlighting opportunities for exploring higher dimensions, materials, and experimental validation.

We employ standard quantum field theory techniques to compute the two-loop effective potential for a supermultiplication of three-forms and demonstrate its equivalence to the AdS5xS5 superstring background effective potential. This result confirms the matching of the corresponding quantum corrections arising from the effective field theory of three-forms and the low-energy string theory effective field equations. In addition, our findings establish the consistency of AdS5xS7 three-form supergravity with previous high precision string theory calculations.

Object-oriented programming languages are increasingly utilized for developing high-performance applications on GPUs, yet existing general graph memory allocators fail to fully leverage these platforms' specific architectural traits. This paper introduces DynaSOAr, a unified memory allocator that bridges this gap by syncing with the GPU's global bus for optimized memory access and deferring allocations to coincide with free cycles for enhanced parallelism. DynaSOAr also employs multiple pointers within allocation nodes to reduce fragmentation. Our benchmark results demonstrate that DynaSOAr delivers superior performance and lower allocation overhead compared to current general-purpose GPU memory allocators.

We examine three $U(1)_X$ gauge theories derived from string compactification, which place the standard model into a larger $U(3) \times U(1)_X$ framework. These frameworks arise from breaking an original $SO(10)$ gauge symmetry, where the residual $U(1)_X$ serves as an exact symmetry prohibiting any Majorana mass for the right-handed neutrino $\nu_R$. Assuming $\nu_R$ exists within the fundamental representation of $U(1)_X$, we analyze the phenomenology under the assumption that $U(1)_X$ breaks at the PeV scale, generating a right-handed neutrino mass via a mechanism of type I seesaw. This scenario accommodates the lightest neutrino mass within the established experimental bounds. Furthermore, we investigate the flavor structure of the resulting neutrino mixing matrix. Our findings demonstrate that these models naturally produce a large mixing angle for $\theta_{13}$ alongside other standard model parameters, and notably, they generate a minimal mixing angle $\theta_{12}$.

This paper presents an analytical study of a straw conduit subjected to uniform internal pressure, a common model for biological systems such as xylem vessels and phloem. The study examines the stability of axisymmetric deformations under plane strain conditions and compares these findings with previous work by Audenheimer. Notably, the paper identifies an additional domain of stability associated with non-uniform deformation modes that was overlooked by Audenheimer. An axisymmetric conduit is further shown to transition abruptly to significant non-axisymmetric distortions at a critical pressure level. The predicted critical pressure for this transition aligns closely with experimental results obtained for straws by Postle and Murch.

When addressing uncertainty in probabilistic circuits, our approach targets the computational determination of robustness metrics like sturdiness and credibility. This is achieved by formulating these problems as linear optimization tasks solved through loose approximation. We introduce a technique for loosely approximating differentiable and structurally exact circuits, allowing for the efficient and parallel computation of values for arbitrarily large networks. Our methodology is validated on credal Bayesian networks using both synthetic data and real-world applications, with results demonstrating superior performance against existing exact algorithms.

We investigate the vibrational modes of a Bose condensate suprasolid exhibiting both translational and spin vibrational degrees of freedom. By deriving a block-diagonal representation of the second-order Hamiltonian, we obtain the equations of motion for a system of $N$ interacting particles in three dimensions. Analyzing these equations in an infinite-$N$ limit yields a spectrum featuring a continuous band overlaid with discrete delta-function peaks, characteristic of a suprasolid. Furthermore, we derive the equations of motion in first-order approximation to demonstrate that discrete vibrational modes correspond to Bloch oscillations.

In a generalized quadrilateral $\mathcal{Q}$, a code $C$ is defined as neighbor-transitive if its local neighbors around any point form a single orbit under the action of $\mathcal{Q}$'s automorphism group. This article characterizes neighbor-transitive codes by linking them to partial spreads and providing specific examples, including those based on generalized quadrangles of mixed tangent-overtangency types. Our findings reveal a bijection between these codes and generalized partial spreads; notably, the associated invariants—the packet size and orbit count—correspond to the size of the packet count and the number of packet spreads, respectively. We validate this by constructing codes derived from user-generated graphs, point sets of specific geometry, and tangent configurations of elliptic curves over finite fields of characteristic 2.

The spatial alignment of star-forming regions within the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) of the Milky Way is primarily influenced by galactic-scale tidal and differential rotation forces. Although prior research has largely relied on 3D correlation techniques, this study introduces a method based on the 2D spatial arrangement of dense clouds to investigate their spatial alignment. This approach utilizes data from a CO survey (10-12 lines) and a 12CO/13CO survey, covering a region of approximately 300 square degrees. Our findings indicate that the mean 2D correlation length is roughly 20 parsecs, which is significantly lower than the typical 50 to 100 parsecs reported using 3D methods. Furthermore, the alignment of clouds in the North and South Central Molecular Zone exhibits a stronger positive correlation than in the inner CMZ. We also observed that the mean 2D correlation length in the inner CMZ is reduced by a factor of approximately 2 compared to the outer zones. This study suggests that the strong tidal forces prevalent in the inner CMZ disrupt spatial coherence among dense clouds, resulting in a shorter 2D correlation scale. Consequently, the application of 2D spatial correlation analysis offers valuable insights into the galactic-scale environment of the CMZ.

We introduce a novel framework analyzing time-resolved absorption data by modeling excited electron groups and their interactions with core holes and one another via mutual rates. This approach accounts for non-linear effects and absorption variations caused by high-intensity sources. The validity of this model is confirmed through comparisons with both empirical evidence and simulation data, specifically regarding the L-edge of Lithium and the K-edge of Chlorine.

This study introduces a temperature sensor featuring an on-chip PTAT (Proportional To Absolute Temperature) circuit with self-calibration capabilities. Designed for a broad operating range of 0.6V to 1.8V, the device achieves a high precision of 0.24°C and a total accuracy of ±1.4°C. Digital output data is delivered via a 14-bit serial interface, supported by a compact physical footprint of merely 1.0mm × 1.0mm. Fabricated using a standard 0.18μm CMOS process, the chip consumes as little as 11.8μA during continuous operation and offers an efficient energy consumption rate of 1.06nJ per conversion cycle.

Photons prepared in a product state of polarization entanglement, where individual photons are uncorrelated, represent an ideal resource for quantum information processing. However, achieving this state using only linear optical components is infeasible. This study demonstrates a practical method to generate a product state of high-fidelity polarization entanglement, beginning with photons in a correlated state (specifically, a two-photon Fock state). We show that applying the "quantum scissors" technique—truncating a two-mode squeezed vacuum via linear optics—effectively prepares the required uncorrelated product state. Furthermore, incorporating an auxiliary single-photon source and a beam splitter enables the creation of another ideal resource: a high-fidelity three-photon Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger (GHZ) state, starting from a correlated GHZ-type state. These findings suggest that utilizing quantum scissors to manage photon correlations offers a promising pathway for quantum resource engineering and quantum state purification.

Classifying IoT gadgets is essential for enabling software-defined services, yet existing auto-discovery techniques fail to account for individual device capabilities. This study presents a new method using machine learning to classify device types while specifically minimizing the number of expenses (sensor readings) incurred during the IoT space analysis. By applying feature selection algorithms to a real-world dataset, the model achieves high accuracy of 94.6% while substantially reducing the average reading count from 10.4 to just 2.8 per device, offering a pathway for more cost-effective and efficient dynamic identification of gadget functions in smart environments.

We introduce a method for aligning bilingual data during its collection. Our approach leverages outside references to align terms within individual queries, achieving performance comparable to advanced query-based alignment tools. Specifically, our system maps the vocabulary in both parallel queries and documents, thereby enriching data alignment even when dealing with query-only pairs that lack document context. We demonstrate the utility and effectiveness of this technique using our dual-language search engine infrastructure to realign an existing collection. Results show significant improvements in downstream tasks, including information retrieval and term alignment itself. The code for our project can be found on GitHub at https://github.com/jianzhong-zhang/term-alignment.

This work introduces a novel algorithm designed to generate Nash equilibria in finite games, leveraging a distorted form of the Brueckner resolver operated within the simplex. For the modified parameter values, the author demonstrates that the method converges linearly to a Nash equilibrium using results derived from the application of a monotone, distorted distance function on the simpleton. Furthermore, it is shown that the Brueckner method represents a specific case of this proposed approach when the relevant parameters revert to their standard settings.

This study introduces a framework for visualizing matter distribution around primordial black holes (PBHs), treating them as shadow regions devoid of matter while maintaining accurate calculations for gravitational interactions outside the PBH radius. The majority of the computational expense arises from determining gravitational forces; consequently, various methodologies for computing gravitational potentials were assessed to optimize performance. The study evaluates three specific approaches: a traditional method using a conventional scalar potential, a hash-grid method employing an unsigned integer grid where each grid cell holds a single integer identifying the corresponding particle, and a hashed octree method utilizing an integer-based grid derived from an unsigned integer octree of particle locations. The purpose of this research is to assess the trade-offs between these methods regarding both computational accuracy and efficiency, specifically regarding force calculations in these specialized simulations.

We have created a system of rigid, aplanate wedges whose total gravitational potential energy mirrors that of a granular system featuring an inclination angle subject to random splay variation. Our findings reveal that this system exhibits two distinct transition stages akin to those observed in granular layers: the initial stage reflects an apparent angle of repose tied to the average tilt, while the second involves a critical threshold of remobilization governed by the system's tilt range. As energy minimization drives the configuration toward the basic state, the potential energy surface displays characteristic traits typical of complex systems, including multiple local minima and extensive flat regions.

Quantum imaging enables the detection of unobservable phenomena at the single-photon level by leveraging quantum interference. While quantum correlation is typically analyzed using high-repetition-rate lasers that record large photon counts per second, we introduce an imaging approach that functions without them. Instead, we utilize quantum interference between two distinct processes: one involving the generation of photons from an object and the other a continuous quantum pump beam. This method allows us to reconstruct high-fidelity images using practically any level of repetition rate, achieving as few as 100 interference events to single out details in an image. This technique significantly broads quantum imaging applications by using high-rep repetition rate lasers that require quantum correlation analysis to achieve contrast with single photon source materials.

The study of interfacial resistance in liquid foam systems reveals that microbubbles exhibit a pressure dependence on roughness alterations. This phenomenon arises because roughness modifications influence the resistance experienced by soap films separating the bubbles. When roughness increases, this resistance intensifies, requiring a higher gas pressure within the bubbles to achieve mechanical equilibrium. Consequently, the pressure variation reflects alterations in the disjoining pressure acting on the films. Experimental observations confirm that such pressure changes persist across diverse scales of bubble roughness and can be accurately described by a model wherein roughness enhancements elevate film resistance through viscoelastic effects.

Skin cancer is a prevalent and severe malignancy that necessitates early detection to prevent metastasis and fatal outcomes. Conventional diagnosis relies on a pathologist's examination of biopsy samples under a microscope, a process that demands extensive expertise and time. Consequently, this study introduces a computational framework to expedite and enhance the accuracy of identifying skin cancer lesions. First, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is employed to automatically classify images into seven specific categories of lesions. Second, a domain adaptation method is applied to mitigate class imbalance inherent in the dataset. Third, a designated outlier identifier is integrated to flag anomalies arising from incorrect classifications or labeling errors. Finally, to ensure interpretability, a feature importance technique elucidates which characteristics drive the CNN's decision-making. This approach effectively automates the diagnosis of cutaneous lesions while maintaining high precision.

We conducted a time- and angle-resolved photoemission study on sodium using photon energies of 2.15, 2.75, and up to 6 eV. By examining electrons with kinetic energies near 10 eV and observing their lifespans, we investigated how these time scales vary with excitation energy. Our findings align with theoretical predictions regarding the lifetime of quasiparticles in sodium, demonstrating that such models can be directly validated through measurements of photemitted electron lifespans.

This research introduces a novel approach for partition function computation that bypasses the traditional limitations of nonequilibrium nonequilibrium (NE) methods, specifically the dependency on altering phase space volume and calculating the Jacobian determinant. By employing a newly defined observable, the study derives a general nonequilibrium formula applicable to systems with both constrained and unconstrained degrees of freedom, even across complex manifolds. A distinctive feature of this methodology is its ability to determine Jacobian determinants utilizing solely surface-based data, eliminating the need for explicit knowledge of Hamiltonian dynamics. Furthermore, the proposed framework integrates several optimization strategies to enhance computational efficiency. On both simulated and real datasets, this method is demonstrated to be both robust and highly effective.

The paper introduces a specific type of diagram known as an accordion, which serves as a visual representation for isomorphism classes containing circulant graphs that possess a Hamiltonian property. These graphs are further linked to partial quadruple graphs and to partitions of sets that are not necessarily complete. We provide a detailed examination of the structural characteristics of these diagrams, which enables us to prove a significant result: every order of up to 800 can generate an isomorphism class of circulant graphs. In addition, our analysis extends the definition of these diagrams to accommodate up to 800 graphs. We also explore how these graphs relate to each other in terms of their mutual relationships. Our findings demonstrate that these graphs are not only unique but also have a specific relationship with each other in terms of their order and structure.
